'''Dana S. Richards''' is a writer, mathematics popularizer and Associate Professor in [[Computer Science]] at [[George Mason University]].

His research interests include comparisons of [[protein sequences]], [[Steiner tree problem|Steiner tree algorithms]],<ref>[https://www.worldcat.org/oclc/316565524 The Steiner tree problem] Authors: Frank Hwang, Dana Richards, Pawel Winter;North-Holland, 1992 {{ISBN| 9780444890986}}</ref> information dissemination in networks, parallel heuristics, methodology for computationally intractable problems and parallel algorithms for median filters.<ref>[https://dl.acm.org/profile/81100452568 Dana S Richards, George Mason University, National Science Foundation]  [[Association for Computing Machinery]] Digital Library</ref> He is the longtime bibliographer of polymath [[Martin Gardner]].<ref name=biblio/>

==Education and career==
Richards received an M.S. from the [[University of Virginia]] in 1976<ref name=bio/> and a Ph.D. in computer science from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] under [[Chung Laung Liu]] in 1984.<ref>[https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=132750 Dana Richards] at the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]</ref>

He was an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at the University of Virginia,<ref name=bio/> and a Program Director of [[Theory of Computing]] at the [[National Science Foundation]]  (June 1993 through May 1994).<ref>[https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=9313063 Awards] National Science Foundation</ref>

He has written or edited seven books<ref>[https://www.isbns.ws/author/Dana_S_Richards Books by Dana Richards] ISBN.NET</ref> and numerous journal articles.<ref>[https://dblp.org/pid/31/6598.html Dana S. Richards] Computer Science Bibliography at [[DBLP]]</ref> In addition, he is a reviewer for many journals, and has received numerous research awards. He became an Associate Professor of Computer Science at George Mason University in 1994.<ref name=bio>[https://cs.gmu.edu/~richards/ Dana Richards] GMU: Biosketch</ref>

==Martin Gardner==
Dana Richards was a friend of Martin Gardner going back to the 1970s,<ref name=byu>[https://math.byu.edu/?event=dana-richards-george-mason-university Speaker:&nbsp;Dana Richards] [[Brigham Young University]], Mar 22nd 2018</ref><ref name=mgbio>[http://www.martin-gardner.org/pix/mg-biography.pdf Martin Gardner:  A Documentary  by Dana Richards] martin-gardner.org</ref><ref>Richards, Dana (2018). ''[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DcjoYvyYkvo Martin Gardner, Annotator]'' G4G13, April 2018 - video</ref><ref name=NPR>[https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=127095954 The Legacy of Math Writer Martin Gardner] ''[[All Things Considered | NPR:  All Things Considered]]'',  May 24, 2010</ref> and in his writing and speaking he often memorialized and popularized Gardner's work.<ref>[https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/meeting-of-the-puzzlers/ Meeting of the Puzzlers:  Hundreds get together to celebrate Martin Gardner and recreational math] By Dana Richards, Scientific American, June 2014</ref><ref>[http://cardcolm.org/Pics/MGJ%202014_10%20SciAm%20MulcahyRichards.pdf Math Games of Martin Gardner Still Spur Innovation] By Colm Mulcahy and Dana Richards, Scientific American, October 2014</ref>
In 2006 he edited ''The Colossal Book of Short Puzzles and Problems'' which collected all of Gardner's short puzzles in one volume.<ref>Dana Richards (Editor), Martin Gardner (Author), [https://wwnorton.com/books/9780393061147 The Colossal Book of Short Puzzles and Problems], W. W. Norton, {{ISBN|978-0-393-06114-7}}</ref> He wrote Gardner's obituary in ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]''<ref>[https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1194002 RETROSPECTIVE:  Martin Gardner (1914–2010)] [[Science (journal)|Science]], 09 July 2010, Vol. 329, Issue 5988, pp. 157</ref> and in 2023 he published a comprehensive bibliography of Gardner's works.<ref name=biblio>
[https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/123180094-the-bibliography-of-martin-gardner The Bibliography of Martin Gardner] Dana Richards (editor), [[Donald Knuth|Donald E. Knuth]] (foreword), June, 2023, Pub: [[Stanford_University_centers_and_institutes#Center_for_the_Study_of_Language_and_Information|Stanford Center for the Study of Language and Information]], {{ISBN|1684000327}}</ref>

Since Gardner's death in 2010 events called [[Celebration of Mind]] are held every October which include games, magic and puzzles in the Gardner tradition, and Richards is frequently featured at these events discussing Gardner's life and work.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o4c6yd5n7bA Algorithmic Puzzles and Martin Gardner] Dana Richards CoM Oct 2020, Jan 22, 2021</ref>

==Books==
* ''The Bibliography of Martin Gardner'', June, 2023<ref name=biblio/>
* ''Dear Martin / Dear Marcello: Gardner and Truzzi on Skepticism'' by Dana Richards, April 28, 2017<ref>''[https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/suppl/10.1142/10345/suppl_file/10345_intro.pdf Dear Martin Dear Marcello: Gardner and Truzzi on Skeptic]'' WorldScientific, p. 10</ref>
* Problems in sorting and graph algorithms   OCLC 12048476 
* ''The colossal book of short puzzles and problems''  {{ISBN|0393061140}}
* ''The Mathemagician and Pied Puzzler'' {{ISBN|156881075X}}
* Dana Richards, "Martin Gardner: A 'Documentary' ", in The Mathematician and the Pied Puzzler: A collection in tribute to Martin Gardner (1999), ed.
